text:
maya: Heads-up — landed a first pass of quantization recommendations for the optimize toolkit and pushed branch `quant/rec-2026` to staging.

tom: Nice. Where's the PR? I want to skim for batching/caching interactions.

maya: PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/862. Main changes: L2 quant profiles, suggested default batch sizes per profile, and KV-cache hinting. Comments explain heuristics.

sasha: @maya quick Q — do the batch-size suggestions assume continuous batching? Will they break low-latency configs?

maya: Two profiles shipped: `latency-first` (batch=1, prefix-cache disabled by default) and `throughput` (batch=32, prefix-cache enabled). The PR has a matrix explaining when each should be picked.

ken: Code-review pinged. I'll take a look today. Do we have kernel fallback tests for tiled kernels?

maya: Added a smoke test at `ci/inference/quant_smoke.sh`. Example run:
```
./ci/run_smoke --profile=latency-first --model=gpt-3-small
```

infra-bot: build 9842 succeeded for branch `quant/rec-2026` (staging). :white_check_mark:

sasha: Potential blocker — Dedicated autoscaler will reject `batch=32` for small dedicated pools. We need a fallback routing policy.

maya: Agreed. Proposal: routing rule that if `pool_throughput < 200 req/s` enforce `max_batch=8` and fallback to `quant-int8-compat` model variant. I'll add this as a canary step.

ryan: Who owns implementing the routing rule and rollout? Need to track ownership so Platform PMs can update runbooks.

maya: Ownership plan: @ken to own the crate changes & PR, @sasha to approve routing policy and autoscaler constraints, @ryan to update deployment docs and runbooks. I'll update `OWNERS` in the repo as part of the PR.

ken: I'll add a detailed rollout plan in the PR: canary 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% with metric gates (p90 latency, token-cost).

ops-elena: Please add an SLA-regression alert to the evals dashboard — we want an automatic rollback if p90 latency increases >200ms or token-cost delta >5%. Also include `deployment=canary-quant` tag on metrics.

maya: Will add eval key `slo_quant_latency_v1` and the token-cost alert. ETA EOD.

tom: Quick FYI — I'm seeing a small staging regression on token-cost for prompt-batching scenario: `cost_delta=+0.03 token_delta=+0.7%`. Logging in PR comments.

maya: Thanks — will investigate today. Suspect prefix-cache eviction thresholds and prebatching heuristics causing slight duplicate tokens.

sasha: Small ask: add a fallback knob in runtime that forces `prefix_cache=false` when `max_batch<=8` so we can avoid cache/latency interactions on small pools.

maya: Good idea — I'll add the runtime flag and wire it into the routing rule.

ops-elena: If rollback occurs, ensure logs include `release=quant/rec-2026` and metric tag `deployment=canary-quant` to make postmortem easier.

maya: Noted and will add. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ken: I'll post review comments by EOD and add the canary gating steps.

ryan: I'll update the runbook and ping support to watch `canary-quant` channel during rollout.

maya: Final note — added cross-team checklist to PR description: QA smoke pass, SLO alert, OWNERS update, runbook link, and rollback command (one-liner).

tom: Thanks — let's keep async updates here.

ops-elena: 👍 monitoring on standby.
